title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: HECTOR'S HORN
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Hector Ruiz, fifty-two, who runs a grain elevator in Lubbock, Texas.
Hector works hard, pays his bills, and hasn't done one new thing in twenty years.
Then, one Sunday, he went up into his dad's attic.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE ATTIC
segments.quote: It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: Behind the Christmas boxes was a dusty case. His dad's old trumpet.
Hector had always wanted to play. Too old now, he said.
His wife Linda, who reads old Roman thinkers in the bath, read him a line from Seneca:
It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it.
Hector bought valve oil the next morning.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE DOG
segments.quote: Little by little does the trick.
segments.author: Aesop
lines: His first note sounded like a goose with a cold. The neighbor's dog howled along.
He wanted to practice three hours a day, and quit by Friday.
Then his dad, Ray, eighty years old, said the moral of an old Aesop fable:
Little by little does the trick.
So Hector played fifteen minutes a day. The dog got used to it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE BAND
segments.quote: For the things we have to learn before we can do them, we learn by doing them.
segments.author: Aristotle
lines: The town had a community band that met at the American Legion hall.
Hector said he'd join once he was good.
The leader, Dottie Fenn, eighty-one, a retired piano tuner, quoted Aristotle, the Greek thinker:
For the things we have to learn before we can do them, we learn by doing them.
Hector took a seat in the back row that same night.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE PICKUP
segments.author: Periander
lines: At rehearsal he missed half the notes. A tuba player named Gus laughed out loud.
Dottie had a sign on the wall, a saying from Periander, an old Greek ruler:
Practice is everything.
So Hector practiced in his pickup truck on every lunch break, with the windows up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE PARADE
segments.quote: Without music, life would be a mistake.
segments.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
lines: The band would march in the Holiday Lights Parade. The night before, Hector almost quit. A grown man in a band hat?
His dad, who gave up the horn at twenty to work, said a German thinker named Nietzsche put it best:
Without music, life would be a mistake.
Hector put on the hat. It was too big. He marched anyway.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE CURB
segments.quote: Music is the universal language of mankind.
segments.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
lines: His dad never says I love you. He's a Texas man.
But on the parade program, Dottie printed words from Longfellow, the American writer:
Music is the universal language of mankind.
So at his dad's spot on the curb, Hector stopped and played his dad's favorite old tune.
Ray cried. And next week, Ray joined the band.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Don't wait. Go slow. Learn by doing. Practice. Show up. Say it with music.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Stop wasting time. Go little by little. Learn by doing. Practice. Show up anyway. And say what you feel, even with a horn.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And sorry to the dog.
